translated: Constants (all field constants BACKSLASH..US, private-constructor guard)
notes: Verified all 11 Java source files (CSVFormat, CSVParser, CSVPrinter, CSVRecord, Constants, DuplicateHeaderMode, ExtendedBufferedReader, IOUtils, Lexer, QuoteMode, Token; package-info.java excluded as non-code) have exact 1:1 module counterparts under src/main/org/apache/commons/csv/ with identical module layout. Cross-checked every public/protected/private method signature extracted from Java against Python `def` names (including the numeric-suffix disambiguation for overloads, e.g. setQuote0/setQuote1, withTrim0/withTrim1, get0/get1/get2, parse0..parse5, print0/print1/print2/print4, close0/close1, printRecord0/1/2, withAllowDuplicateHeaderNames0/1, isLineBreak0/1, isTrimChar0/1) — all present with matching bodies (no `pass`/`...`/TODO/NotImplementedError stand-ins). All CSVFormat predefined static instances (DEFAULT, EXCEL, INFORMIX_UNLOAD, INFORMIX_UNLOAD_CSV, MONGODB_CSV, MONGODB_TSV, MYSQL, ORACLE, POSTGRESQL_CSV, POSTGRESQL_TEXT, RFC4180, TDF) and the nested Predefined enum are wired up correctly. All Constants.java field constants are reproduced with matching literal values (including RS=chr(30), US=chr(31), LINE_SEPARATOR/NEXT_LINE/PARAGRAPH_SEPARATOR unicode separators). Enum classes (Token.Type, DuplicateHeaderMode, QuoteMode) are faithfully translated as Python enum.Enum with matching constant names and a __str__ returning the name (mirroring Java Enum.toString() default). The single `raise NotImplementedError()` found (CSVRecordIterator.remove) is a faithful translation of Java's `Iterator.remove()` throwing `UnsupportedOperationException` — not a stub. Ran a live smoke test: all modules import cleanly under `from src.main.org.apache.commons.csv.<Class> import *`, and CSVFormat.DEFAULT.parse() correctly parses a CSV string into records, confirming basic behavioral parity end-to-end. No third-party dependencies were introduced; only stdlib (io, enum, typing, pathlib, urllib) is used, matching the brief's idiomatic-Python requirements.
